flagged.title: Kingship, Succession and Ruling England in Richard's Absence
flagged.reason: The video states that Richard returned from the Holy Land in 1193 to appoint Hubert Walter (when he was actually imprisoned in Germany until 1194) and claims Richard heavily levied the Saladin Tithe, both of which teach incorrect specification facts and contradict lesson assessment.

mark_affecting.quote: But when Richard returned from the Holy Land in 1193, he made a game-changing appointment: Hubert Walter.
Then he heavily levied the Saladin Tithe... Richard hammered it home before he finally sailed away

flagged.title: The Loss of Normandy: Château Gaillard and 1204
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly dates the Treaty of Le Goulet to 1199 both in narration and on screen, whereas the lesson and the Edexcel specification explicitly date it to 1200.

mark_affecting.video_says: In 1199, that Treaty of Le Goulet bought a very tense peace (and timeline slide displays '1199: Treaty of Le Goulet')
mark_affecting.lesson_says: the 20,000-mark relief and ceded territory of the 1200 Treaty of Le Goulet

flagged.title: Royal Government and Finance under John
flagged.reason: The video repeats debunked figures and claims for William FitzAlan's relief fine (£7,000 rather than 10,000 marks) and misstates the historical novelty of the 1207 tax.

mark_affecting.quote: Just consider this staggering number: £7,000. That is the devastating relief fine John levied on one single baron, a guy named William FitzAlan.
It was the very first English tax assessed on someone's whole personal wealth, rather than just the land they owned or their feudal status.

flagged.title: Runnymede 1215: Magna Carta and the First Barons' War
flagged.reason: The video states that John executed many of the surrendered noble defenders at Rochester Castle, when in fact only one crossbowman was executed and the rest were imprisoned, which directly impacts mark schemes.

mark_affecting.quote: instead of showing customary chivalric mercy to the surrendered noble defenders, John executed many of them.
